intervals.label: relocation, reassembly and commissioning at Fermilab (MC-1)
intervals.quote: In 2013, Brookhaven's magnetic storage ring was transported from Long Island, New York, to Fermilab in Batavia, Illinois.

intervals.label: Run-1 through Run-6 data taking
intervals.quote: over the six data-taking periods, or runs, from April 2018 to May 2023

name: Muon g-2 storage ring
notes: technology_classes uses 'other': no listed technology_class in the ontology enum (lar_tpc, water_cherenkov, ... haloscope, spectrometer, other) specifically names a muon storage ring; 'spectrometer' was considered but the ring's function (long-term storage in a precision magnetic field, not momentum analysis) is a poorer fit than the generic 'other' with a descriptive `technology` string.

diameter.quote: The resulting ring had a central orbit radius of 7.112 m

magnetic_field.quote: B0 needed to be well below saturation and was chosen to be 1.45 T.

summary.plain: A 14-metre ring of superconducting magnet, originally built at Brookhaven and moved to Fermilab, that holds spinning muons in a very uniform magnetic field while detectors around its rim watch them wobble.
summary.technical: Superferric muon storage ring (7.112 m central orbit radius, 14.224 m diameter, 1.45 T field), the same magnet used in BNL E821, relocated to Fermilab in 2013 and instrumented with 24 calorimeter/tracker stations around its inner radius for the Muon g-2 (E989) precession measurement.

technology.quote: The resulting ring had a central orbit radius of 7.112 m, and 24 detector stations were placed symmetrically around the inner radius of the storage ring.
technology.value: Superconducting superferric muon storage ring with 24 electromagnetic calorimeter stations and straw tracking detectors around its circumference
